title: Spectral signatures of hidden order and hidden quantum critical points
authors: Reja H. Wilke, Henning Schlömer, Sebastian Paeckel, Annabelle Bohrdt, Fabian Grusdt
abstract: Hidden-order phases elude the conventional Ginzburg-Landau framework: although they spontaneously break symmetry, their order remains invisible to standard local two-point correlators. Instead, they are typically characterized by nonlocal (string) order parameters and are believed to underlie a range of exotic quantum states, such as symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. While hidden correlations have previously been detected through nonlocal observables in quantum gas microscope experiments, in realistic solid-state systems multipoint observables are typically inaccessible and the signatures of hidden order remain largely unexplored. In this work, we show that hidden order in doped spin chains can be directly probed through dynamical two-point response functions measurable by resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and neutron scattering. Focusing on a minimal model, we numerically identify clear spectral fingerprints of both the hidden-order phase, its associated hidden quantum critical point as well as a specific group of gapless SPT phases. Complementing our numerical results with analytical insights, we uncover the microscopic origin of these spectral signatures and demonstrate how they emerge from the interplay between spin and charge degrees of freedom. Together, our results establish spectroscopy as a practical probe of hidden order and gapless SPT phases and provide a unified understanding of the low-energy physics governing these unconventional quantum phases.
summary: This work demonstrates that hidden-order quantum phases, which defy detection by standard local measurements, can be spectroscopically identified in doped spin chains. By analyzing the dynamical spin structure factor using the TFIM model, the authors map out the phase diagram and predict characteristic spectral fingerprints for both the hidden order phase and gapless topological states. This establishes spectroscopy as a powerful, practical tool for probing exotic quantum matter.
main_problem: Hidden-order phases, which break symmetry but lack conventional local order parameters, are difficult to study because their order is characterized by nonlocal (string) parameters.
main_result: The authors show that the spectral signatures of hidden order and gapless SPT phases can be directly probed using dynamical two-point response functions measurable by RIXS and neutron scattering.
method: The study employs numerical techniques like matrix product states and analytical methods such as the squeezed space construction to analyze the dynamical spin structure factor.
model_or_system: The investigation focuses on the doped transverse field Ising model (TFIM), a minimal model exhibiting a strong interplay between spin and charge degrees of freedom, analyzed in the context of the $t_1-t_2$-Fermi-Hubbard Model.
key_observables: Dynamical two-point response functions, specifically the dynamical spin structure factor ($\hat{S}_z(q, \omega)$), and the squeezed space staggered magnetization ($M^*_S$).
important_parameters: Doping concentration, transverse field strength ($h_x$), and hopping amplitudes ($t_1, t_2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that the dynamical structure factor can be decomposed into components related to charge and spin fluctuations, and uses continuum approximations in some calculations.
figures_summary: Figures compare local vs. hidden order parameters ($M_S$ vs $M^*_S$) across phase diagrams, and show the distinct spectral fingerprints (e.g., linear dispersive branches, $	ext{K}_0$ forms) of the hidden order and gapless SPT phases.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the difficulty of detecting hidden order using local correlators. It then applies the model to the doped TFIM, using the squeezed space formalism to define hidden order parameters. Finally, it calculates and analyzes the dynamical structure factor using advanced spectral techniques to map out the phase diagram and identify spectral fingerprints.
why_interesting: The connection drawn between spectroscopic measurements (RIXS/neutron scattering) and abstract theoretical concepts like hidden order and SPT phases provides a concrete, measurable pathway for experimental condensed matter physicists.
